name: MonarchBottomSheet
title: Sheet
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (window, scrim, drag, back, predictive back, motion) with a Monarch surface, handle and header; androidx.compose.material3.ModalNavigationDrawer for a start-side panel
summary: A modal panel from the bottom: MonarchBottomSheet is the MonarchBottomSheet with the Monarch surface, handle and header. The platform keeps dragging, back and the motion.
whenToUse: For a task that belongs to the current screen and needs more room than a dialog: a form with a header and a footer, details of a row, settings for a view. At expanded width, for a panel that sits beside the content, use a supporting pane (see peek-panel).
whenNotToUse: Not for a short question: use MonarchDialog (see dialog). Not for a list of actions: use MonarchMenu. Not for the app's destinations: use a navigation drawer (see sidebar-nav).
api: @Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called when the sheet has closed: swipe, back, scrim, the handle or dismiss().

options.name: title
options.description: The heading at 18/600, also the pane title.

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the title in the muted text colour.

options.name: dismissible
options.description: Whether a swipe, back and the scrim close it; dismiss() always does.

options.name: fullyExpanded
options.description: Opens fully expanded, or half open first when the content is tall.

options.name: fullWidthContent
options.description: The content spans the sheet for list rows with their own 16dp padding; the header then starts at 16dp.

options.name: content
options.description: The content; call dismiss() to slide the sheet away from a button.

states.name: expanded
states.description: With skipPartiallyExpanded = true the sheet opens at the height of its content, up to nearly the full screen.

states.name: partially expanded
states.description: Without it, a tall sheet opens at half the screen and the person drags it up.

states.name: closing
states.description: A drag down, a tap on the scrim or back calls onDismissRequest; hide the sheet with sheetState.hide() before you stop composing it, so it animates out.

states.name: busy
states.description: dismissible = false keeps it open while work runs; dismiss() in the content still closes it.

appearance: The raised background (a lighter step than the screen in a dark theme) with 16dp top corners and no shadow, a 36 by 4dp handle in the subtle text role centred in a 48dp target, the title at 18/600 and the description at 14 in the muted text role, 20dp at the sides and under the content. The scrim is the overlay scrim role.
platformNotes: The web Sheet attaches to any edge (end by default) and has sizes sm to full, a header, body and footer, a close button, a drag handle and a busy state. On Android a modal sheet comes from the bottom: the sizes are the expanded and partially expanded states, the handle is showHandle, busy is dismissible = false, the header is title and description, and the body and footer are ordinary content; dismiss() in the content closes the sheet with its motion. The web's start-side sheet is a ModalNavigationDrawer; there is no end-side modal sheet in Material 3 for Compose, so at expanded width use a supporting pane instead (see peek-panel). iOS uses the system sheet and the inspector.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the title as the pane title and as a heading when the sheet opens.
The handle is a named 48dp button with the Dismiss action (and Expand or Collapse when half open), so closing never needs a drag.
Back dismisses it unless dismissible is false.
The title wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Call sheetState.hide() and stop composing the sheet in invokeOnCompletion; removing it at once skips the closing animation.
The keyboard pushes the sheet up; keep the confirm button visible by putting it before a long content or making the content scroll.
On a tablet the sheet is limited to sheetMaxWidth (640dp) and centered.
